# Packages Folder Guidance

- `pkgs/` contains reusable Python package code.
- Favor clean module boundaries, reusable abstractions, and library-style APIs over one-off scripts.
- Keep package changes independent from local machine assumptions unless a package is explicitly meant to handle them.
- Prefer testable utilities and stable interfaces for analysis and automation code.
- **Polars only for DataFrames:** library interfaces accept and return `polars.DataFrame`, never pandas and
  never a union of both. Callers convert themselves. See `spec/pkgs/dataframes.md`.

## `ds` CLI Conventions

- For commands under `pkgs/ds/cli/`, use Typer for CLI definitions.
- For command/process execution under `pkgs/ds/cli/`, use `run_cmd` from `ds.cli.util`.
- Keep `pkgs/ds/cli/` command patterns separate from OS automation patterns under `.os/`.
- For CLI commands that sync a "database"-like file (eg a parquet file synced from scraping), write to a fixed
  output path (no `--out` flag) and confirm before overwriting via `typer.confirm(...)`, printing the resulting
  DataFrame first.
- Settings are exposed via `ds.settings.get_settings()`. Always call this function rather than importing `SETTINGS`
  directly (`from ds import SETTINGS` / `from ds.settings import SETTINGS`) — `set_settings()` rebinds the module
  global, so a previously-imported name won't see later updates.

## `ds/data` Conventions

`pkgs/ds/data/` is this repo's "database": each parquet file directly under it (eg `char.parquet`,
`framedata.parquet`) is a table, and rows/columns should be reasoned about the way you would reason about a SQL
table (primary key, foreign keys, grain), not as an arbitrary data dump.

- `pkgs/ds/data/*.parquet` are the synced "database" tables; `pkgs/ds/data/raw/` holds the scraping scripts and any
  hand-copied source data used to produce them.
- **External sources: one place, one vocabulary.** All code that calls another site or API lives under
  `pkgs/ds/data/`, and its public functions take and return this repo's standards (`char_id` for a fighter
  and `char_group` for a character-select pick, both from `char.parquet`, `char_icon`, UTC datetimes, shared field names), never a site's own ids. Read
  `spec/pkgs/ds/data/external_sources.md` before adding or changing a source; it has the rules for mapping a
  site's character names to `char_id` and a table of where each source stands.
- `pkgs/ds/data/*.parquet` are tracked via Git LFS (see root `.gitattributes`, `*.parquet filter=lfs diff=lfs
  merge=lfs -text`), not committed as regular git blobs. Requires `git-lfs` installed (`brew install git-lfs` +
  `git lfs install`) on any machine that will commit/pull these files.
- Parquet is preferred over CSV for these tables: it's typed (no schema re-inference on read) and, for this mostly
  string/repetitive data, compresses far smaller than CSV (verified: `framedata.csv` at 431KB became a 104KB
  `framedata.parquet` — about 4x smaller; feather/Arrow IPC was tried too but came out *larger* than CSV since it's
  uncompressed by default, so parquet is the right choice here, not feather).
- `pkgs/ds/data/README.md` is the data dictionary for every table in `pkgs/ds/data/`. Whenever a change adds,
  renames, or removes a column produced by `pkgs/ds/data/raw/*.py` or `pkgs/ds/cli/data.py`, update that README in
  the same change so its column tables stay accurate.
- Document each table's primary key, foreign keys into other tables, and grain in that README, plus a runnable
  join example (eg polars), so the tables can be queried like relational tables.
- Name foreign key columns `{table}_id`, where `{table}` is the referenced parquet file's name without extension
  (eg `framedata.parquet` references `char.parquet` via a `char_id` column, not `character`).
- ultimateframedata.com is static HTML (semantic classes like `.movecontainer`, `.movename`, `.startup`) — no JS
  rendering/headless browser needed, plain `httpx2.get()` + BeautifulSoup works. Its roster page
  (`https://ultimateframedata.com/smash`) lists characters as `.charactericon` divs with `<a href="/{slug}">`;
  filter out the non-character `stats` link. Prefer scraping fresh character slugs over trusting old hand-copied
  ids, since site slugs can differ (eg `donkey_kong` not `dk`, `king_dedede` not `king_ddd`).
- supermajor.gg (player character/stage usage, `pkgs/ds/data/raw/supermajor.py`, agent tools in
  `pkgs/ds/ai/supermajor.py`) is server-rendered Next.js: data is JSON in the RSC payload, not HTML classes, and
  tag search uses the site's public search key, committed in that file. Read the "Site notes" comment at the top
  of it (findings, decisions, dead ends, how to update the key) before changing it.
  Its player pages are blocked by the site's bot check since Nov 2026; only its tag search is still used.
- start.gg (sets, games, characters, stages, tournaments, entrants; `pkgs/ds/data/raw/startgg/`, derived stats
  in `pkgs/ds/data/startgg/`, agent tools in `pkgs/ds/ai/startgg.py`) is an official
  GraphQL API, not a scrape. Read the "Site notes" at the top of `client.py` before changing it. Rules:
  - **Two layers.** `ds/data/raw/startgg/` is the API as it is: one function per query, normalization only
    (char ids, datetimes, paging). Anything computed (usage, head-to-head, aggregates) goes in
    `ds/data/startgg/`.
  - **Results stay out of the agent, not out of the data.** The data layer returns everything, including
    winners, scores, seeds and placements. Agent tools (`ds/ai/`) must not expose a result field, function or
    parameter. `ds/data/startgg/results.py` is Python-only and never imported by `ds/ai`;
    `tests/ds/ai/test_startgg_capability.py` enforces all of this. What was left out is listed in the NOTE at
    the top of `pkgs/ds/ai/startgg.py`.
  - **Token:** `get_settings().startgg_api_token` (keyring, set with `ds settings sync`; env
    `STARTGG_API_TOKEN` wins). Limits: 80 requests / 60 s, 1000 objects / request.
  - **Tag what comes from its docs** with `# ds::external-source:` (see
    `.agents/skills/external-review/SKILL.md`), so the review skill can re-check it.
- New secrets (API keys, tokens) are a `Settings` field stored in the keyring and prompted for by
  `ds settings sync`, like `pydantic_gateway_api_key`. Never a committed value or a loose `.env`.
- smash-tube.com (YouTube match video search, `pkgs/ds/data/raw/smashtube.py`, agent tool in
  `pkgs/ds/ai/smashtube.py`) is server-rendered PHP: plain HTML per video, characters sent as Japanese names
  (`SITE_CHARACTER` maps `char.id` to them), and the result page answers 403 without browser-like headers. Read
  its "Site notes" comment (site behavior, what's allowed, what's still unverified) before changing it.
- Use `httpx2` (Pydantic's actively maintained continuation of `httpx`, same API) as the HTTP client, not `httpx`.
- Before writing any new scraper, verify whether the target site is static HTML or JS-rendered (fetch raw HTML and
  check for the data) before assuming a headless browser is needed.

## pydantic-ai Conventions

Applies to pydantic-ai tools, capabilities and agents (eg `pkgs/ds/ai/`). Reference implementations:
`pkgs/ds/ai/knowledge.py`, `pkgs/ds/ai/smashdb.py`.

- **Return Pydantic models from tools whose results have a fixed shape**, not `dict` / `list[dict]`. Give
  every non-obvious field a `Field(description=...)`. For example, `list_docs -> list[DocInfo]` and
  `find_character -> list[Character]`.
- **Send return schemas for model-returning tools.** Register them as `Tool(fn, include_return_schema=True)` in
  the capability's `tools=[...]`. Return schemas are off by default, and without one the model only learns the
  result shape by calling the tool.
- **Return tables as `TableResult`** (`ds.ai.table`), not `list[dict]` or a DataFrame. This covers query
  results, per-move frame data, and anything with many rows or columns that vary per call.
  - Build it with `TableResult.from_df(df, max_rows=...)`. The model reads compact CSV (about 1/3 the tokens
    of JSON records), plus `rows`/`total_rows`/`truncated`.
  - Python gets the exact DataFrame back with `.to_df()`, dtypes included.
  - `tables_from_messages(result.all_messages())` pulls every table out of an agent run. It also works on
    messages loaded back from JSON.
  - A raw DataFrame can't be returned from a tool: pydantic-ai fails to serialize it.
  - Register these tools with `include_return_schema=True` too.
- **Return `str` when the model needs text as-is**, eg line-numbered doc text for `path:line` citations
  (`read_doc`).
- **Tool docstrings are the model's only guidance for arguments.** Document every argument (the `Args:` section
  becomes the parameter descriptions), with an example value.
- **Validation errors:** raise `ModelRetry` with an actionable message (valid ids, available headings) rather
  than returning an error value.
- **Failures a retry can't fix:** raise `ToolFailed`, not `ModelRetry`, when the call is done and has failed
  (the site is down or blocking us, an HTTP error, a missing resource). `ModelRetry` makes the model call
  again, and a second failure exceeds the tool's retry budget, which ends the whole run with
  `UnexpectedModelBehavior` instead of an answer. `ToolFailed` shows the model the failure so it can tell the
  user. Example: `_run` in `pkgs/ds/ai/startgg.py`.
- **Keep results small:** cap row and character counts (eg `MAX_ROWS`, `MAX_SEARCH_HITS`) so a broad call
  doesn't flood the context window.
- **Package domain tools as a `Capability`** with `defer_loading=True`, so its instructions and tool
  definitions only enter context when relevant.

## Outside Calls: `ds.util.http` / `ds.util.graphql`

Every request to an outside site or API goes through these two wrappers, never `httpx2` directly
(`tests/ds/util/test_http.py` fails on a direct `httpx2.get/post/request` call under `pkgs/`).

- `with http.request(method, url, source=..., name=..., **httpx_kwargs) as (resp, call):` (async:
  `async with http.arequest(...)`). Plain httpx2 underneath; pass `client=` to reuse a connection. Add what
  only the caller knows to `call`, eg `call["rows"] = len(matches)`. The response isn't checked: call
  `resp.raise_for_status()` inside the block, so a failure is the record's `error`.
- `await graphql.gql(url, query, variables, source=..., headers=..., extensions=..., check=...)` for
  GraphQL: returns status + body; `check` raises the API's own errors inside the record.
- Each call logs one record (`ds.util.logging.log_call`): the full request with secret headers filtered
  (`http.SECRET_HEADERS`; add a new auth header name there), the response's status, type, size, `cf-ray` /
  bot-check headers and the start of an error body, timing, and for GraphQL the operation, variables,
  query, rows / page info and `errors`. SmashGPT's debug panel (Alt+D) shows them, with copy-as-curl.
- Wrap work that makes many calls in `log_group("<name>")` so its records share a `group` id (start.gg's
  `player_sets` and the agent tools' `_run` do).
- Agent tool calls: `ds.ai.call_log.ToolCallLog` (in `ds.ai.agent`'s capabilities) logs each call as a timed
  'tool' record and puts its `tool_call_id` on every record made inside it, which is how an app links a
  request back to the tool call (SmashGPT's debug log does).
- The wrappers only send and log. Retries, rate limits and anything cache-like stay with each source
  (caches need the user's approval first, see "Caching Policy" in `.agents/agents.md`).

## Tests Against External APIs

Tests never spend real requests (start.gg allows 80 per 60 s per token, shared with the app).

- **Recorded, not live.** A test that needs a real API answer is a `@pytest.mark.vcr` test
  (pytest-recording / VCR.py, which supports `httpx2`); it replays a cassette under `tests/<area>/cassettes/`.
  For anything else, fake the transport (`httpx2.MockTransport`) or the client function.
- **Network blocked by default:** `--block-network` is in pytest's `addopts` (root `pyproject.toml`), so a plain
  `uv run pytest` can't reach the internet, and a `vcr` test with no recording fails instead of calling out.
- **Re-recording is a deliberate act:** `uv run pytest <test file> --record-mode=rewrite` with a stored token.
  Keep recordings small (eg 20 sets, not 150), and only public data.
- **No secrets in cassettes.** `tests/conftest.py`'s `vcr_config` filters the `Authorization` header and stores
  bodies decompressed so they can be read. Before staging a cassette, grep it for the token and for
  `authorization` / `bearer` / `cookie`; only response CORS headers may mention `Authorization`.
- A test that replays with a fake token takes the real one only while recording (see `recorded_token` in
  `tests/ds/data/test_startgg_api.py`).

## Docs-Derived Code

Code whose values or rules come from Smash facts in `docs/` (constants, thresholds, rules like "grabs ignore
armor") is linked to the docs in both directions, so readers see where a value came from and docs edits find the
code to update. Plain logic doesn't need this.

- **Tag it in code**, on the line(s) above the constant or function, pointing to a MyST label (stable across
  rewording, unlike headings or line numbers):

  ```python
  # ds::docs-source: docs/moveset.md#sl-armor-modifiers (sync-tested)
  SHORT_HOP_ATTACK_MULTIPLIER = 0.85
  ```
  - Uses the repo's `ds::` tag prefix (see `.agents/agents.md`, "Repo Tag Prefix"). A bonus: ruff's ERA001
    reads a plain `# docs: docs/...` as commented-out code, but `ds::` isn't valid Python, so it's never
    flagged.
  - Use `# ds::docs-source: none yet (...)` for a fact that has no docs page yet.
  - **No discrepancy tags in code.** Whether a value is provisional is tracked only in `docs/`: the page's
    `% ds::discrepancy: D-###` lines (ID only) and `docs/scratch/discrepancies.md`. Resolving one changes the docs,
    and the rule below then leads to the code.
- **Back-link on the docs page:** one `% ds::research: code: <file> (<names> <- <label>) -- sync-tested in <test>`
  line per file that depends on it.
- **Sync-test numbers:** put the number in its own cell of a labelled list-table and assert it in
  `tests/ds/calc/test_docs_sync.py` with `ds.util.docs.docs_table("<label>")`. A docs edit then fails
  `uv run pytest tests/` and names the constant.
- **When a docs page changes** (edited directly or by resolving a discrepancy), find the code built on it with
  `grep -rn "ds::docs-source: docs/<page>.md" pkgs tests` plus the page's `% ds::research: code:` lines, update it in
  the same change, and run `uv run pytest tests/`.
